model.note: Both the original commercial survey agent and its backfill ran on Opus.

boundaries.note: The 27 Aug OpenConnector spike was EXECUTED_CLEANED under prior authorization. Its receipts are cited, not re-run. Nothing was executed in this run.

denominator_note: The commercial packet stopped at 18 rows under a hard usage limit, named its 14 unreached surfaces, and was closed by a targeted Opus backfill that prioritised the single most load-bearing omission (Stripe's idempotency contract) first. Nothing was padded.

smoke.method: Structural validation over every packet file: JSONL parsed line by line, required fields asserted, duplicate and mis-prefixed IDs checked, top10 re-derived from disposition, decision-ledger JSON parsed after manual edits.

self_correction.original_draft: Replay with the same key and a different payload is a hard error; non-2xx is not cached
self_correction.correction: Stripe's documented behaviour is the OPPOSITE of the second clause: it saves the status code and body of the first request regardless of whether it succeeds or fails, and returns cached 500s on replay.
self_correction.origin_of_error: The claim came from a secondary summary of the Stripe rule in the hono-idempotency README and did not survive reading Stripe's own documentation.
self_correction.disposition: Invariant amended with the correction left visible; the caching choice is now flagged as a deliberate Actionist decision rather than an inherited default.

headline_claims_challenged.claim: Idempotency has no production OSS supply
headline_claims_challenged.challenge: Is a 14-star top result evidence of absence or of a bad search?
headline_claims_challenged.resolution: Corroborated from two independent directions: the OSS search found a field of many single-author repos pushed within months of each other, and the commercial survey independently found no embedded-iPaaS or agent-action vendor documenting a write idempotency-key contract. Two different populations, same gap.

headline_claims_challenged.claim: Adopt OpenConnector's catalogue and OAuth engine, never its store
headline_claims_challenged.challenge: Is the store genuinely unfit or merely unfamiliar?
headline_claims_challenged.resolution: Unfit by demonstration rather than inference: the 27 Aug spike created two tenant connections and retrieved both under one admin token, and the schema read confirmed no tenant column, service-only OAuth config keying, and a hardcoded salt.

headline_claims_challenged.claim: Stripe is the contract to copy
headline_claims_challenged.challenge: Copying a payments contract into a general action runtime may import assumptions that do not hold.
headline_claims_challenged.resolution: The critical caveat was surfaced rather than smoothed: rate limiters run BEFORE Stripe's idempotency layer, so a 429 can produce a different result under the same key. This became a new invariant (INV-P11-11) about where Actionist's own layer must sit, not a blanket endorsement.

licence_flags.finding: BSL 1.1, licensor now IBM; bars hosted or embedded competition with paid versions. OpenBao is the MPL-2.0 Linux Foundation fork and the answer.
SSPL-1.0 with an Apache-2.0 future grant; section 13 forces publication of the entire service-management stack if offered as a service. Most likely to be mistaken since it markets heavily as OSS.

BSL 1.1 with a nuance in our favour: forbids a public platform where third parties register their own service deployments, while permitting production deployments invoking services the licensee wrote. Conditional, not disqualified.
Elastic License 2.0 behind a click-through preamble; forbids providing the software to third parties as a hosted service. Best functional fit in its category, which is what makes it dangerous.
MIT with an ee/ carve-out; each adopted feature needs a path check.
NOASSERTION because mid-relicence MIT to Apache-2.0; contributions without relicensing consent remain MIT, so provenance is per-file.
Apache-2.0 on the CLI only while the event gateway is closed SaaS - structurally the same trap as Composio.
AGPL-3.0 with section 13 triggering on network use.
